units.text: Title 1 Par3 regulates Rac1 signaling and microtubule organization during planar polarization of auditory hair 2 cells 3 4 One sentence summary: Par3 regulates planar polarity of auditory hair cells
Introduction

The sense of hearing and balance is critically dependent on the sensory hair cells of the inner ear. Hair cells 35 are specialized epithelial cells that are polarized along both the apical-basal axis and within the plane of the 36 epithelial cell sheet, referred to as planar cell polarity (PCP). Importantly, the hair bundle, the 37 mechanotransduction organelle atop auditory hair cells, adopts a planar-polarized structure with rows of 38 stereocilia arranged in a staircase-like V shape, and thus is directionally sensitive to mechanical stimuli

Interestingly, in the maculae, the transcription factor Emx2 has been shown to reverse hair bundle polarity in its . In this study, we found that Par3 regulates PCP but 77 not apical-basal polarity in the OC. Par3 is asymmetrically localized in the OC during PCP establishment.

Deletion of Par3 disrupted microtubule organization and basal body positioning, leading to hair bundle polarity 79 and orientation defects. Surprisingly, Par3 has distinct localizations from its canonical partner Par6/aPKC and 80 is not required for asymmetric localization of LGN/Gi; instead, we present evidence that Par3 regulates 81 microtubule cortical capture in hair cells through a Tiam1-Rac-Pak axis.

Schwander et al., 2010). Furthermore, planar polarity of the hair bundle is coordinated at the tissue-level in all 40 sensory epithelia. In the hearing organ, called the organ of Corti (OC), hair bundles are uniformly oriented with 41 the vertices of the V pointing to the lateral edge. On the other hand, in the maculae hair bundles show mirror-42 image polarity along the line of polarity reversal (LPR), which enable detection of movements in opposite 43 directions (Deans, 2013). 44 45 These features of planar polarity are established during development, under genetic control by a multi-tiered 46 signaling hierarchy. Upon hair cell differentiation, a cell-intrinsic machinery controls the migration and 47 positioning of the kinocilium (and the associated basal body) at the lateral pole, where it is tethered to the 48 nascent hair bundle and induces elongation of adjacent stereocilia. Multiple signaling modules of the cell-49 intrinsic machinery have been discovered, including the small GTPase Rac1 and its effector p21-activated 50 kinase (Pak) (Grimsley-Myers et al., 2009; Sipe and Lu, 2011), cdc42 and its downstream effector aPKC 51 (Kirjavainen et al., 2015), as well as LGN/Gαi/dynein (Ezan et al., 2013; Sipe et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013), 52 a complex with an evolutionarily conserved role in mitotic spindle orientation. It has been suggested that these 53 modules act in concert to provide subcellular landmarks and spatially control cortical capture of centriolar 54 microtubules during kinocilium/basal body positioning, thereby influencing hair bundle morphogenesis and 55 orientation.

organ level, an evolutionarily conserved non-canonical Wnt/PCP pathway mediates intercellular 58 signaling between hair cells and supporting cells to coordinate hair bundle orientation (Goodrich and Strutt, 59 2011; Lu and Sipe, 2015). Components of this pathway include the "core" PCP genes, homologs of Drosophila 60 Frizzled, Van Gogh (Vangl1 and Vangl2), Flamingo (Celsr1-3), Dishevelled (Dvl1-3), Prickle and Diego, as well 4 as vertebrate-specific PCP genes, such as Ptk7 (Lu et al., 2004) and Scrib1 (Montcouquiol et al., 2003).

These tissue-64 level regulators are not required for intrinsic bundle polarity, suggesting that the cell-intrinsic machinery can 65 polarize individual hair cells independent of tissue polarity cues. However, how this is achieved at the 66 molecular level and the precise mechanisms by which global PCP signals impinge on the cell-intrinsic 67 machinery is incompletely understood. 68 69 To address these questions, here we investigated the role of Par3 (Pard3, Mouse Genome Informatics) in hair 70 cell PCP. Par3 encodes a PDZ-domain scaffold protein and is an evolutionarily conserved regulator of cell 71 polarity (Macara, 2004). Central to its function in establishment of cell polarity, Par3 can self-associate to form 72 oligomers and bind to membrane phospholipids and a diverse range of cell polarity and cytoskeletal regulatory 73 proteins (Chen and Zhang, 2013). In mammalian epithelial cells, Par3 is localized to tight junctions, where it 74 regulates the separation of apical and basolateral membrane domains (Macara, 2004). In Drosophila 75 neuroblasts, the cortical Par3/Par6/aPKC complex recruits the LGN/Gi/NuMA complex, thereby aligning the 76 mitotic spindle to the cellular polarity axis (Yu et al., 2000)

Previous studies have demonstrated that 06 uniform hair bundle orientation in the OC is controlled by both tissue-level and cell-intrinsic PCP signaling, 07 while kinocilium positioning within the hair bundle is mediated by cell-intrinsic PCP signaling (Lu and Sipe, 08 2015). In the control, hair bundles were uniformly oriented along the mediolateral axis of tissue polarity, with 09 the kincocilium found at the vertex of the V-shaped hair bundle (Figure 3A, C). By contrast, a significant 10 number of hair bundles in Par3 cKO were misoriented (Figure 3B, D). Moreover, some had a flattened 11 morphology, with the kinocilium positioned close to the edge of the hair bundle (Figure 3E, arrows; 3F)anchored at the lateral pole in a planar polarized manner (Sipe and Lu, 2011). In contrast, many 16 Par3 cKO hair cells have mis-positioned centrioles that correlated with hair bundle misorientation (Figure 3H). 17 Moreover, alignment of the two centrioles along the mediolateral axis was also disrupted (Figure 3J-M, 18 arrows). Together, the kinocilium/basal body positioning and hair bundle orientation defects demonstrate a 19 requirement of Par3 in both cell-intrinsic and tissue-level PCP establishment in the OC.

We therefore examined the localization of Par6 and aPKC in the developing OC. In 39 contrast to Par3, we did not observe significant junctional localization of Par6 or aPKC in either control Par3 cKO OC, the planar-polarized localization patterns of Par6 and aPKC in hair cells 43 were still present albeit with decreased staining intensity, and the asymmetric crescents at hair cell-supporting 44 cell contacts were misoriented in accordance with the disorganized cellular mosaic in the OC (Figure 5K, L, O, 45 P). Thus, during PCP establishment Par6 and aPKC had localization patterns similar to each other but distinct 46 from and largely independent of their canonical partner Par3, suggesting that Par3 has separate functions from Par6/aPKC during PCP establishment in the cochlea.

In other systems, Par3 controls Rac1 activity by directly 76 interacting with Tiam1 (Chen and Macara, 2005; Nishimura et al., 2005; Pegtel et al., 2007). To determine 77 whether Par3 interacts with Tiam1 in vivo in the developing cochlea, we performed co-immunoprecipitation (IP) 78 experiments using pooled lysates of E16.5 wild-type cochleae. Indeed, Par3 was detected in the 79 immunoprecipitates of anti-Tiam1 but not control antibodies, indicating that Par3 and Tiam1 form a complex in 80 vivo in the developing cochlea (Figure 7C). 81 82 To further determine the functional significance of Par3-Tiam1 interaction in the cochlea, we examined Tiam1 83 localization in the Par3 cKO cochlea at E17.5. In the control, Tiam1 was localized to the cytoplasmic microtubule 84 network and the kinocilium (Figure 7D-H). In Par3 cKO , while Tiam1 was still detected on the microtubules and 85 the kinocilium, the staining intensity was significantly reduced (Figure 7I-M). Taken together, these results 86 suggest that Par3 regulates Tiam1 localization and/or activity during PCP establishment in the cochlea. 87 88 Par3 regulates kinocilium positioning through microtubule organization and stability in the cochlea 89 Having established that Par3 regulates Rac-Pak signaling, we next sought to uncover the cellular events 90 controlled by Par3 during PCP establishment in the cochlea. Accumulating evidence suggests that 91 kinocilium/basal body positioning is achieved through interactions between the dynamic hair cell microtubule 92 network and the hair cell cortex(Sipe et al., 2013; Sipe and Lu, 2011). In the control cochlea, there was significant 04 enrichment of EB1 staining around the lateral hair cell cortex (Figure 9A, C, arrows), consistent with the idea 05 that cortical polarity factors stabilize microtubule attachment at the lateral hair cell cortex. In contrast, EB1 06 staining was diffuse throughout the apical cytoplasm in Par3 cKO hair cells, suggesting that microtubule cortical 07 attachment was not stabilized at the lateral hair cell cortex in the absence of Par3 (Figure 9B, D). Together, 08 these results suggest that Par3 promotes a dynamic microtubule network and microtubule cortical attachment 09 at the lateral hair cell cortex to control kinocilium positioning and hair bundle orientation.

hair cell-intrinsic polarity through Rac-Pak signaling 28 Deletion of Par3 in the inner ear resulted in defects in both hair bundle orientation and morphogenesis, 29 indicating that it is a component of the cell-intrinsic polarity machinery, which regulates the microtubule-cell 30 cortex interactions that anchor the kinocilium/basal body at the lateral pole of the hair cell. Multiple signaling 31 modules regulating aspects of this process have been revealed by genetic analysis in mice, including the 32 laterally enriched Rac1-Pak signaling and Gi/LGN/dynein complex, as well as the medially enriched 33 Par6/aPKC complex. Interestingly, Par3 appears to act separately from its canonical polarity partners during 34 PCP establishment in the cochlea. At the onset of hair bundle morphogenesis, Par3, but not Par6 or aPKC, is 35 asymmetrically enriched on the lateral hair cell cortex. As development proceeds, Par3 and Par6/aPKC are 36 enriched in separate domains in hair cells. This is in contrast to C. elegans zygotes, Drosophila neuroblasts 37 and mammalian epithelial cells. One possible mechanism of regulating the dynamic interaction between Par3 38 and Par6/aPKC is Par3 protein phosphorylation (Nagai-Tamai et al., 2002; Nakayama et al., 2008). Likewise, 39 Par3 is required for cortical recruitment of LGN through the inscuteable adaptor protein during asymmetric cell 40 division (Williams et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2000). In turn, the cortical LGN/Gi/NuMA complex interacts with 41 dynein to generate pulling forces on astral microtubules and align the mitotic spindle with the cell polarity axis 42 (di Pietro et al., 2016)

deletion significantly decreased Rac1-Pak activity levels in the developing cochlea, indicating a 45 role in regulating Rac1 GTPase signaling. This Par3-Rac1-Pak signaling axis has been reported in other 46 developmental processes (Tep et al., 2012), indicating that it is a conserved mechanism for regulation of cell47polarity. In the developing cochlea, we found that the Rac GEF Tiam1 is highly expressed in hair cells and 48 forms a complex with Par3 in vivo. Tiam1 localization to hair cell microtubules and kinocilia is regulated by 49 Par3. Of note, we did not observe significant overlap in the localization patterns of Tiam1 and Par3 in the OC, preferentially detect the inactive, auto-inhibited pool of Tiam1, and that binding of Par3 at the lateral 53 cortex may release Tiam1 autoinhibition thereby activating Rac1. In support of a role of Tiam1 in PCP 54 establishment, treatment of cochlear explants with NSC23766, which inhibits Tiam1-mediated Rac activation, 55 led to kinocilium/basal body positioning defects (Sipe and Lu, 2011). Based on these findings, we propose that 56 Par3 regulates both the localization and activity of Tiam1 to promote local Rac1 activation during microtubule-57 mediated planar polarization of hair cells.

Par3 regulates microtubule dynamics and organization in the OC59 Loss of Par3 disrupted the organization of hair cell microtubule network and cortical capture of microtubules at 60 the lateral hair cell cortex, accompanied by increased levels of acetylated tubulin. The precise mechanisms by 61 which Par3 regulates microtubule dynamics remain to be determined. Par3 has been shown to associate with 62 dynein and regulate microtubule dynamics in cultured cells (Schmoranzer et al., 2009). Although we were 63 unable to detect this association in the cochlea by co-IP assays (data not shown), it remains possible that Par3 64 directly or indirectly regulates dynein motor activity, which in turn controls microtubule dynamics (Goldspink et 65 al., 2017; Hendricks et al., 2012). Par3 may also regulate microtubule dynamics through interactions with 66 additional GEFs for Rho family GTPases (Liu et al., 2004; Moore et al., 2013) 67 Par3 integrates cell intrinsic and intercellular PCP signals 68 We have shown that asymmetric Par3 localization (this study) and localized cortical Rac-Pak activity are 69 regulated by the core PCP gene Vangl2 (Grimsley-Myers et al., 2009). Thus, tissue-level intercellular PCP 70 signaling coordinate hair bundle orientation through spatial regulation of the intrinsic cell polarity regulators. Of 71 note, Par3 cortical localization per se is not dependent on tissue-level PCP signaling, and may instead be 72 mediated by binding to membrane phospholipids (Krahn et al., 2010) and/or the Nectin-family of cell adhesion 73 molecules (Takekuni et al., 2003).

The crosstalk between intercellular and cell-intrinsic PCP signaling at multiple levels ensures the robust 82 integration of cell-intrinsic and tissue polarity signaling in the OC.

Distinct mechanisms of PCP establishment in different sensory end organs 84 Similar to auditory hair cells, hair bundles of vestibular hair cells also have a planar polarized staircase pattern 85 and are coordinately oriented. Tissue-level intercellular PCP signaling coordinates hair bundle orientation in 86 both auditory and vestibular sensory epithelia (Deans, 2013). By contrast, there are different requirements for 87 the cell-intrinsic polarity machinery in the OC and maculae. In the maculae, the heterotrimeric G proteins act 88 downstream of Emx2 to effect polarity reversal in the Emx2-expressing domain, but this is not required for the 89 "default" planar polarity (Jiang et al., 2017). In addition to Par3, the microtubule-based motors kinesin-II and 90 dynein are also dispensable for PCP in the utricle (Sipe et al., 2013; Sipe and Lu, 2011), suggesting that PCP 91 in the maculae is predominantly mediated by an actin-based mechanism.
